features.name: Responsive iframes
features.description: The frame-sizing CSS property sets the size of an <iframe> element to that of it contents, to avoid scrolling in the iframe. Embedded documents allow this with the <meta name="responsive-embedded-sizing"> element and request resizing in the embedding page by calling window.requestResize().

features.name: Fullscreen API
features.description: The fullscreen API makes a specific element fill the whole screen and hides most browser UI.

features.name: @function
features.description: The @function CSS at-rule defines a custom function that takes CSS values or custom properties as arguments, and returns a CSS value. It can be based on conditional logic such as by using the @media at-rule.

features.name: Functions
features.description: Functions are series of statements that can be called and return a value. The function keyword (as in function () { }) and arrow (=>) expression create functions. The JavaScript functions protocol includes default and rest parameters and binding to this.

features.name: Gamepad
features.description: The navigator.getGamepads() API accesses and responds to signals from game controllers.

features.name: Gamepad haptic feedback
features.description: The gamepad.vibrationActuator property represents a gamepad's haptics hardware, which allows you to control the vibration motors in a gamepad.

features.name: Gamepad touch buttons
features.description: The touched property of a GamepadButton object indicates whether a button capable of detecting touch is currently touched.

features.name: Gamepad VR hands and poses
features.description: The hand and pose properties of a Gamepad object represent the position in space and the hand that WebVR controllers are held in.

features.name: Gamut mapping
features.description: Colors in CSS and <canvas> elements can be defined out of range of an output device or the color space of the canvas. Gamut mapping brings the color into range while preserving hue and lightness.

features.name: Gap decorations
features.description: The column-rule and row-rule CSS properties display decorative lines between columns and rows of a flex, grid, or multi-column layout. The rule-break, rule-outset, and rule-paint-order properties control the appearance of these lines.

features.name: Generators
features.description: Generator functions (function*) create iterators that return multiple values, one after another, on-demand.

features.name: Geolocation API
features.description: The navigator.geolocation API requests the user's latitude, longitude, heading, and speed.

features.name: <geolocation>
features.description: The <geolocation> HTML element represents a button that, upon activation, prompts the user to choose whether to grant the page access to geolocation data.

features.name: getComputedStyle()
features.description: The getComputedStyle() global method returns an CSSStyleDeclaration object that represents all CSS declarations applied to a given element.

features.name: IndexedDB getAllRecords()
features.description: The getAllRecords() method of IDBObjectStore and IDBIndex return records and their primary keys from an IndexedDB store or index. The records can be read in batches and in reverse order. The getAllRecords() methods speed up read operations on large datasets.

features.name: getBoxQuads()
features.description: The getBoxQuads() method, when called on a document, element, pseudo-element, or text node, returns the list of DOMQuad objects that represent the CSS boxes used to render the node.

features.name: getHTML()
features.description: The getHTML() method of Element and ShadowRoot objects serializes an element's DOM to an HTML string.

features.name: Map getOrInsert()
features.description: The getOrInsert() and getOrInsertComputed() methods of Map objects get a value, setting and getting a default value if needed.

features.name: GIF
features.description: The GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) image format is a raster graphics file format with animation and lossless compression.

features.name: globalThis
features.description: The globalThis property accesses the global this value (and hence the global object itself) across environments.

features.name: Global privacy control
features.description: The Sec-GPC request header indicates that the user does not consent to a website or service selling or sharing their personal information with third parties.

features.name: Gradient interpolation
features.description: Gradient interpolation controls how the colors between gradient stops are calculated in CSS. For example, linear-gradient(to right in oklch longer hue, red, red); calculates in the oklch color space, with the hue going all the way around the hue circle from red back to red.

features.name: Gradients
features.description: The linear-gradient() and radial-gradient() CSS functions and their repeating counterparts create backgrounds that progress smoothly between multiple colors.

features.name: Grid
features.description: CSS grid is a two-dimensional layout system, which lays content out in rows and columns.

features.name: Grid animation
features.description: Grid animation allows you to animate the grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows CSS properties.

features.name: Grid lanes
features.description: The display: grid-lanes and display: inline-grid-lanes CSS declarations create a layout where items are tightly packed in parallel lanes. Items are placed one by one in the lane that has the most available space. Also known as masonry.

features.name: Gyroscope
features.description: The Gyroscope API reads the angular velocity of a device in three dimensions.

features.name: Hanging punctuation
features.description: The hanging-punctuation CSS property puts punctuation characters outside of the box to align the text with the rest of the document.

features.name: hardwareConcurrency
features.description: The navigator.hardwareConcurrency property is the number of logical processors available to run threads on the user's computer.

features.name: :has()
features.description: The :has() CSS functional pseudo-class matches an element if any of the selectors passed as parameters would match at least one element.

features.name: :has-slotted
features.description: The :has-slotted CSS pseudo-class matches <slot> elements where the fallback content is not shown. The pseudo-class matches any slotted content, including white space, text nodes, or elements.

features.name: Hashbang comments
features.description: The #! comment at the absolute start of a script or module is treated as a normal comment and is ignored by the JavaScript engine.

features.name: hashchange
features.description: The hashchange event fires when the URL fragment identifier (the part of the URL starting with #) of the current page has changed.

features.name: <head>
features.description: The <head> element contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, such as the title, <script> and <style> elements, and <meta> elements.

features.name: <header> and <footer>
features.description: The <header> and <footer> HTML elements represent content that precedes and follows the main page content, respectively.

features.name: Heading offset
features.description: The headingoffset HTML attribute offsets the heading level of descendant <h1>–<h6> elements. The headingreset HTML attribute prevents heading offset computation from traversing beyond the element.

features.name: Heading pseudo-classes
features.description: The :heading and :heading() CSS pseudo-classes match headings of varying levels. The :heading pseudo-class matches any heading (<h1> through <h6>). The :heading() selector matches any of the given levels. For example, :heading(1, 2) matches headings level 1 and 2.

features.name: <h1> through <h6>
features.description: The <h1> through <h6> HTML elements represent six levels of section headings, in order of decreasing importance.

features.name: <hgroup>
features.description: The <hgroup> element represents a heading and related content.

features.name: hidden="until-found"
features.description: The hidden="until-found" attribute hides an element until it is found using the browser's find-in-page search or it is directly navigated to by following a URL fragment.

features.name: Custom highlights
features.description: Custom highlights style arbitrary text ranges, without adding extra elements to the DOM.

features.name: Custom highlights from point
features.description: The CSS.highlights.highlightsFromPoint() method returns an array of Highlight objects at a specified point.

features.name: History
features.description: The window.history API manipulates the browser session history, from navigations to state management, in the tab or frame that the current page is loaded in.

features.name: Host
features.description: The :host CSS pseudo-class selects the containing element of the shadow tree in which it is used. The :host() CSS pseudo-class selects the that element only if it matches the provided selector.

features.name: <hr>
features.description: The <hr> element represents a thematic break between paragraphs, often shown as a horizontal rule.

features.name: HSL
features.description: The hsl() and hsla() CSS functions pick colors using hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency) channels.

features.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
features.description: The Strict-Transport-Security HTTP response header informs browsers that the site should only be accessed using HTTPS, and that any future attempts to access it using HTTP should automatically be converted to HTTPS. Also known as HSTS.

features.name: <html>
features.description: The <html> element represents the top-level of an HTML document and is referred to as the root element.

features.name: HTML media capture
features.description: The capture HTML attribute for <input type="file"> elements allows the user to capture media using the device's camera or microphone.

features.name: HTML processing instructions
features.description: An HTML processing instruction is text enclosed by <? and >, which marks a target for further processing. They may appear anywhere in a document. They are ignored like comments when they're not recognized for a specific purpose.

features.name: HTML setter methods
features.description: The setHTML(), replaceWithHTML(), beforeHTML(), prependHTML(), appendHTML() and afterHTML() DOM methods, and unsafe equivalents, insert HTML into an existing tree.

features.name: HTML streaming setters
features.description: The streamHTML(), streamReplaceWithHTML(), streamBeforeHTML(), streamPrependHTML(), streamAppendHTML() and streamAfterHTML() DOM methods, and unsafe equivalents, return writeable streams that incrementally insert HTML into an existing tree.

features.name: HTTP authentication
features.description: The Authorization and WWW-Authenticate headers authenticate a user with a server.

features.name: HTTP/1.1
features.description: HTTP/1.1 is a network protocol used by browsers and servers. It has been superseded by HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

features.name: HTTP/2
features.description: The HTTP/2 protocol is a major revision of the HTTP network protocol, providing improved performance and efficiency by using a single TCP connection to send multiple streams of data at once.

features.name: HTTP/3
features.description: HTTP/3 is a major revision of the HTTP network protocol, providing improved performance and efficiency by using QUIC as the underlying transport protocol.

features.name: HWB
features.description: The hwb() CSS function picks colors using hue, whiteness, and blackness channels.

features.name: Hyphenate character
features.description: The hyphenate-character CSS property sets the character or string to use at the end of a line before a line break.

features.name: Hyphenate limit chars
features.description: The hyphenate-limit-chars CSS property sets the number of characters in a word before it is hyphenated and the minimum number of characters on either side of the hyphen.

features.name: Hyphenation
features.description: The hyphens CSS property controls when long words are broken by line wrapping. Although called hyphens, the property applies to word-splitting behavior across languages, such as customary spelling changes or the use of other characters. Support for non-English languages varies significantly.

features.name: <i>
features.description: The <i> HTML element identifies idiomatic content, styling text as italic by default.

features.name: ic unit
features.description: The ic CSS length unit corresponds to the width of CJK ideographic characters.

features.name: Idle detection
features.description: The IdleDetector API is used to notify a webpage of the user's idle, active, and locked state.

features.name: if()
features.description: The if() CSS function is an inline conditional value that returns a value based on a set of conditions.

features.name: <iframe>
features.description: The <iframe> element embeds another HTML page into the current page.

features.name: Credentialless iframes
features.description: The credentialless attribute for the <iframe> HTML element loads third-party content in an ephemeral context and does not send any credentials such as cookies. When using cross-origin isolation, this allows you to embed content that does not send Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy headers.

features.name: Sandboxed iframes
features.description: The sandbox attribute for the <iframe> HTML element sets many security restrictions on the iframe, such as preventing form submissions or opening modal dialogs. Optional allow- values relax specific restrictions.

features.name: srcdoc
features.description: The srcdoc attribute for the <iframe> HTML element sets a string of HTML to embed in the document. The value of srcdoc overrides loading a document from the src attribute.

features.name: image()
features.description: The image() CSS function creates an image similar to url() but with additional functionality. It can create a solid color as an image, provide a fallback from an image URL to a solid color, or clip a sprite image using media fragments. Not to be confused with the Image() constructor.

features.name: Image maps
features.description: The <area> and <map> elements define a clickable area on an image.

features.name: image-orientation
features.description: The image-orientation CSS property corrects the rotation of an image using the image's metadata, such as EXIF.

features.name: image-rendering
features.description: The image-rendering CSS property sets how images are scaled, retaining smoothness for photos, or hard edges for pixel art and QR codes.

features.name: image-set()
features.description: The image-set() CSS function provides a set of images at different resolutions or pixel densities, which the browser can pick from, depending on the device capabilities.

features.name: ImageBitmapRenderingContext
features.description: The ImageBitmapRenderingContext API is the "bitmaprenderer" rendering context for the <canvas> element. It is commonly used to transfer frames from an OffscreenCanvas to a user-visible <canvas> element.
The element adds an image into the document.

features.name: @import
features.description: The @import CSS at-rule loads styles from another stylesheet.

features.name: import defer
features.description: The import defer and import.defer() JavaScript statements import a module while deferring its evaluation until its first use.

features.name: Import maps
features.description: A <script type="importmap"> HTML element provides an import map as a JSON string. An import map controls how the browser should resolve module specifiers when importing JavaScript modules.

features.name: Multiple import maps
features.description: Multiple <script type="importmap"> HTML elements merge to produce the overall import map.

features.name: :indeterminate
features.description: The :indeterminate CSS pseudo-class selects any form element whose state is indeterminate, such as checkboxes that have been set to an indeterminate state with JavaScript, or radio buttons which are members of a group in which all radio buttons are unchecked.

features.name: IndexedDB
features.description: The IndexedDB API is a local storage transactional object database.

features.name: Individual transform properties
features.description: The translate, rotate, and scale CSS properties apply single transformations independently, as opposed to applying multiple transformations with the transform CSS property.

features.name: inert
features.description: The inert HTML attribute marks an element and its descendants as non-interactive. Inert elements don't get focus or fire click events.

features.name: inherit
features.description: The inherit keyword resets any CSS property to the computed value of that property from the parent element.

features.name: initial-letter
features.description: The initial-letter CSS property sets the number of lines the first letter of an element occupies. You can use the property to make a raised capital or drop cap.

features.name: initial
features.description: The initial keyword resets any CSS property to its initial value as defined by the specification. For example, the initial value of the display property is inline, regardless of the element being styled. Not to be confused with revert, which resets to the user or browser default style.

features.name: Ink
features.description: The navigator.ink API uses the system compositor to draw to a <canvas> element ahead of pointer events, reducing the delay between moving a stylus or cursor and a pen stroke appearing on screen.

features.name: <input>
features.description: The <input type="text"> HTML element allows the user to enter information into a form. By default, an <input> element is a text input.

features.name: <input type="button">
features.description: The <input type="button"> HTML element represents a button that triggers some action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog, styled as a labeled rectangular box by default. Not to be confused with the <button> element, which contains HTML content.

features.name: <input type="checkbox">
features.description: The <input type="checkbox"> HTML element represents a tickable box with two states, checked and unchecked.

features.name: <input type="color">
features.description: The <input type="color"> HTML element shows a color picker from which users can choose a color value.

features.name: alpha and colorspace attributes for <input type=color>
features.description: The ability to control the opacity of a color picked using <input type="color"> and determine the colorspace of the selected color.

features.name: Date and time <input> types
features.description: The <input type="date"> and <input type="time"> HTML elements show date and time pickers.

features.name: <input type="month">
features.description: The <input type="month"> HTML element shows a month picker.

features.name: <input type="week">
features.description: The <input type="week"> HTML element shows a week picker.

features.name: Email, telephone, and URL <input> types
features.description: The <input type="email">, <input type="tel">, and <input type="url"> HTML elements represent email address, telephone number, and URL fields in a form.

features.name: input (event)
features.description: The input event fires when a form control changes or an element with the contenteditable attribute changes.

features.name: <input type="file">
features.description: The <input type="file"> HTML element shows a file picker from which users can choose a file to upload with the form.

features.name: <input type="file" multiple>
features.description: The <input type="file" multiple> HTML element shows a file picker from which users can choose one or more files to upload with a form.

features.name: <input type="file" webkitdirectory>
features.description: The <input type="file" webkitdirectory> HTML element shows a file picker from which users can choose a folder to upload with the form.

features.name: <input type="hidden">
features.description: The <input type="hidden"> HTML element represents a form field that is not shown visually but is still included in the form submission.

features.name: <input type="image">
features.description: The <input type="image"> HTML element is an image that can be used to submit a form, like the <input type="submit"> element.

features.name: <input type="number">
features.description: The <input type="number"> HTML element represents numeric input data.

features.name: <input type="password">
features.description: The <input type="password"> HTML element represents a field for users to enter a password. The password is hidden from view, typically replaced by dots or asterisks.

features.name: <input type="radio">
features.description: The <input type="radio"> HTML element represents one button in a group such that only one can be chosen at a time.

features.name: <input type="range">
features.description: The <input type="range"> element represents a slider for choosing an inexact value between a minimum and maximum value.

features.name: <input type="reset">
features.description: The <input type="reset"> HTML element represents a button that sets all form fields to their initial values.

features.name: Input selectors
features.description: The :checked, :disabled, and :enabled CSS pseudo-classes match form elements based on their state.

features.name: <input type="submit">
features.description: The <input type="submit"> HTML element represents a button that triggers an action on its associated <form>, such as sending the form data to a server.

features.name: inputmode
features.description: The inputmode global HTML attribute gives a hint about what type of data is to be entered into an <input> element, such as text, numeric, or email, so the browser may help the user enter data using an adapted input mechanism, such as an on-screen virtual keyboard.

features.name: <ins>
features.description: The <ins> element represents a range of text that has been inserted into a document, styling text as underlined by default.

features.name: Insertable streams for MediaStreamTrack
features.description: The MediaStreamTrackProcessor and MediaStreamTrackGenerator APIs modify the contents of a media track for merging streams, applying real-time effects like funny hats, and content overlays.

features.name: <install>
features.description: The <install> HTML element represents a button that, upon activation, prompts the user to choose whether to install a progressive web app.

features.name: Interaction media queries
features.description: The pointer, any-pointer, hover, and any-hover CSS media queries set styles based on the presence of pointing devices and their ability to hover over elements. For example, most smartphones match the (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) media query.

features.name: Interaction contentful paint performance entries
features.description: An interaction-contentful-paint performance entry measures the duration of an interaction that causes one or more contentful paints. You can use it to measure LCP for soft navigations in single page apps.

features.name: interactivity
features.description: The interactivity: inert CSS declaration makes an element and its descendants inert, like when using the inert HTML attribute. Inert elements can't be focused or clicked, their text can't be selected or found using the browser's find-in-page feature.

features.name: Interest invokers
features.description: Interest invokers, registered by the interestfor HTML attribute, trigger events and actions on a target element when a user shows interest in the element, through behaviors such as hover, focus, or long-press. Pseudo-elements apply styles to sources and targets of interest.

features.name: interpolate-size
features.description: The interpolate-size CSS property sets whether animations and transitions interpolate between a numeric value and a keyword value, such as from a fixed length to auto or fit-content.

features.name: Intersection observer
features.description: The IntersectionObserver API asynchronously observes changes in the intersection of a target element with an ancestor element or with a top-level document's viewport.

features.name: Intersection observer visibility tracking
features.description: The trackVisibility parameter for the IntersectionObserver constructor enables tracking the visibility of an element, to detect if it may be obscured by other content or visual effects. Also known as IntersectionObserver v2.

features.name: Intl
features.description: The Intl API provides language sensitive string comparison, number formatting, date and time formatting, and more.

features.name: Intl.DisplayNames
features.description: The Intl.DisplayNames API provides localized names of language, region, script, and currency codes.

features.name: Intl.DurationFormat
features.description: The Intl.DurationFormat API creates a locale-aware formatter that turns an object representing a duration (such as days, hours, and minutes) into a string.

features.name: Intl.ListFormat
features.description: The Intl.ListFormat API creates a locale-aware formatter that turns iterable objects into localized strings.

features.name: Intl.Locale
features.description: The Intl.Locale API parses Unicode locale identifiers, with language, region, and script codes, such as zh-Hans-CN or en-GB.

features.name: Intl.Locale info
features.description: The getter methods of the Intl.Locale API provide supplemental information about a Unicode locale, such as the locale's calendar (for example, the first day in a week or the weekend start day), writing direction, 12- or 24-hour cycles, and numbering system.

features.name: Intl.PluralRules
features.description: The Intl.PluralRules API creates a locale-aware object that tells you which of the language's pluralization rules apply based on a given number.

features.name: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat
features.description: The Intl.RelativeTimeFormat API creates a locale-aware formatter that turns an object representing a relative time (such as '1 day ago') into a localized string.

features.name: Intl.Segmenter
features.description: The Intl.Segmenter API creates a locale-aware text splitter that can separate a string into meaningful graphemes, words, or sentences.

features.name: inverted-colors media query
features.description: The inverted-colors CSS media query sets styles based on whether the user has inverted all colors, such as with mobile accessibility settings.

features.name: Invoker commands
features.description: The command and commandfor attributes for the <button> HTML element dispatch an action to an element when the button is invoked (by click or keystroke), as a declarative alternative to addEventListener() calls or onclick attribute handlers.

features.name: :is()
features.description: The :is() CSS functional pseudo-class takes a selector list as its argument, and matches any element that can be selected by one of the selectors in that list.

features.name: Error.isError()
features.description: The Error.isError() static method checks whether a value is an Error object.

features.name: isSecureContext
features.description: The isSecureContext global property is a boolean for whether the current browsing context is secure. This is primarily a check that the page has been served over an HTTPS URL.

features.name: isolation
features.description: The isolation CSS property creates a new stacking context, which impacts z-index ordering and blend modes.

features.name: Iterator.concat()
features.description: The Iterator.concat() JavaScript method returns an iterator that yields values from a sequence of iterators, exhausting each iterator before moving on to the next.

features.name: Iterator includes()
features.description: The includes() method of an Iterator object returns true when an item yielded by the iterator is the same as a given value. It's similar to the includes() method of arrays.

features.name: Iterator join()
features.description: The join() method of an Iterator object returns a string concatenation of all the iterator's items, separated by commas or a given separator string. It's similar to the join() method of arrays.

features.name: Iterator methods
features.description: The Iterator object is an abstract base for objects that implement the iterator protocol. It provides methods common to built-in iterators, such as filter(), find(), map(), and reduce(). You can also use the static method Iterator.from() to convert an existing iterable into an Iterator.

features.name: Iterator.zip() and Iterator.zipKeyed()
features.description: The Iterator.zip() and Iterator.zipKeyed() static methods return new iterators that aggregate items from multiple iterables. You can use them to iterate jointly, to get all of the items at the same position in each iterable.

features.name: Iterators and the for...of loop
features.description: The for...of loop operates on a sequence of values sourced from an iterable object, such as arrays, array-like objects, DOM collections, iterators, generators, and user-defined iterables. All built-in iterators inherit from the Iterator class.

features.name: JavaScript (initial core language support)
features.description: JavaScript is a programming language that runs in browsers, usually through the <script> element. JavaScript has changed over many years. This feature represents the oldest language features, such as built-in objects, statements, and operators. Also known as ECMAScript.

features.name: JPEG
features.description: The JPEG image format is a raster graphics file format with lossy compression.

features.name: JPEG XL
features.description: The JPEG XL image format is a raster graphics file format that supports animation, alpha transparency, and lossy as well as lossless compression.

features.name: JavaScript modules
features.description: JavaScript modules allow code to be organized into reusable units. Modules use import to load other modules and export to declare what is available to import from other modules. In HTML, modules are loaded with <script type="module">.

features.name: JavaScript modules in service workers
features.description: The navigator.serviceWorker.register() method accepts { type: "module" } to load scripts that use import and export. Also known as ECMAScript modules or ESM in service workers.

features.name: JavaScript modules in shared workers
features.description: The SharedWorker() constructor accepts { type: "module" } to load scripts that use import and export. Also known as ECMAScript modules or ESM in shared workers.

features.name: JavaScript modules in workers
features.description: The Worker() constructor accepts { type: "module" } to load scripts that use import and export. Also known as ECMAScript modules or ESM in workers.

features.name: JSON
features.description: The JSON API provides static methods for parsing values from and converting values to JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), a serialization format for objects, arrays, numbers, strings, Boolean values, and null.

features.name: JSON import attributes
features.description: Module import … with { type: "json" } statements load JSON data. Also known as JSON module scripts.

features.name: JSON source text access
features.description: To serialize and parse JSON in a lossless way, JSON.stringify() handles rawJSON values and JSON.parse()'s reviver callback takes a source context parameter.

features.name: justify-self in block layouts
features.description: The justify-self CSS property aligns an item along a container's inline axis in block layouts, like it does in grid layouts. Likewise, the justify-items property sets a default justify-self value for all items in a container in a block layout.

features.name: <kbd>
features.description: The <kbd> element represents textual user input, such as keyboard or voice input, styling text in monospaced type by default.

features.name: Keyboard events
features.description: The keydown and keyup events fire for each key press (or, with modifier keys, a combination of key presses) on a keyboard.

features.name: Keyboard lock
features.description: The navigator.keyboard.lock() API allows you to capture keys that are normally reserved by the operating system. It can be used to provide an immersive fullscreen experience such as games.

features.name: Keyboard map
features.description: The navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap() API returns a map from key codes to human readable key names. It can be used to describe buttons to the user when using the keyboard as a set of buttons, such as in games.

features.name: KHR_parallel_shader_compile WebGL extension
features.description: The KHR_parallel_shader_compile extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts checks the status of shader compilation without blocking the runtime.

features.name: Lab and LCH
features.description: The CIE Lab color space expresses colors in terms of lightness and how red/green and blue/yellow a color is. LCH is a variant of Lab with polar coordinates. These color spaces can be used with the CSS color(), lab(), and lch() functions. Also known as CIELAB and CIELCH.

features.name: <label>
features.description: The <label> HTML element represents a caption for a form field.

features.name: :lang()
features.description: The :lang() CSS functional pseudo-class matches elements based on their content language.

features.name: lang
features.description: The lang global HTML attribute defines the language of an element. It's used by assistive technology to correctly read the content, translation tools to select the origin language, and other applications.

features.name: Language
features.description: The navigator.language property is a string representing the preferred language of the user, usually the language of the browser UI. The navigator.languages property is an array of strings representing the user's preferred languages.

features.name: Language detector
features.description: The LanguageDetector API identifies the likely natural language that some text is written in. You can use this API to supplement machine translation when the source source language is not known.

features.name: LanguageModel
features.description: The LanguageModel API prompts an on-device language model. Also known as the Prompt API.

features.name: Largest contentful paint (LCP) performance entries
features.description: A largest-contentful-paint performance entry measures the time it takes for the largest image or text to appear. Largest contentful paint (LCP) is a common metric for perceived loading times.

features.name: Layout direction override
features.description: The unicode-bidi and direction CSS properties override the Unicode layout algorithm. They are intended for Document Type Definition (DTD) designers. For HTML documents, you should use the dir global HTML attribute and <bdo> HTML element instead.

features.name: Layout instability performance entries
features.description: A layout-shift performance entry measures the layout stability of web pages based on movements of the elements on the page. They're used to calculate cumulative layout shift (CLS), a common metric for perceived stability.

features.name: Let and const
features.description: The let and const declarations define block-scoped variables.

features.name: letter-spacing
features.description: The letter-spacing CSS property controls the amount of space between each letter in an element or block of text.

features.name: lh unit
features.description: The lh CSS length unit corresponds to the requested line height, the computed value of the line-height property. Some lines may be higher than this based on their content.

features.name: light-dark()
features.description: The light-dark() CSS function accepts two colors and uses one depending on the current color scheme.

features.name: light-dark() image values
features.description: The light-dark() CSS function accepts, in addition to colors, two <image> values, such as a gradient or URL, and uses one depending on the current color scheme.

features.name: line-break
features.description: The line-break CSS property sets how strictly to apply rules for wrapping text to new lines, especially for symbols and punctuation.

features.name: line-clamp
features.description: The line-clamp CSS property limits the text in a block container to a certain number of lines. The prefixed -webkit-line-clamp is widely supported but only works with -webkit-box-orient: vertical in combination with display: -webkit-box or display: -webkit-inline-box.

features.name: line-height
features.description: The line-height CSS property sets the spacing between text baselines, oriented to the horizontal or vertical writing mode.

features.name: linear() easing
features.description: The linear() easing function for animations and transitions interpolates linearly between the control points, and can be used to approximate complex easing functions, such as a bounce effect.

features.name: <link>
features.description: The <link> element creates a relationship between the current document and an external resource, such as a stylesheet or favicon.

features.name: Link parameters
features.description: The link-parameters CSS property, param() modifier for the url() CSS function, and the #:~:param(…) URL fragment set custom CSS environment variables on an external resource, such as an SVG image, allowing the external resource to adapt its presentation based on the variables.

features.name: <link rel="dns-prefetch">
features.description: The rel="dns-prefetch" attribute for the <link> HTML element is a hint to the browser that the page or user is likely to request resources from another domain, so the browser should preemptively resolve DNS for the href value's domain.

features.name: <link rel="expect">
features.description: The rel="expect" attribute for the <link> HTML element is a hint to the browser to block rendering until the element that the href value references is connected to the document and fully parsed.

features.name: <link rel="preconnect">
features.description: The rel="preconnect" attribute for the <link> HTML element is a hint to the browser that the page or user is likely to request resources from another origin, so the browser should preemptively start a connection to the href value's origin.

features.name: <link rel="prefetch">
features.description: The rel="prefetch" attribute for the <link> HTML element is a hint to the browser that the user is likely to navigate to a resource, so the browser should preemptively fetch and cache the resource.

features.name: <link rel="preload">
features.description: The rel="preload" attribute for the <link> HTML element requests resources, such as images or style sheets, that the page needs soon, so the browser may prioritize them for loading before rendering begins.

features.name: Link selectors
features.description: The :link CSS pseudo-class matches unvisited links, :visited matches visited links, and :any-link matches both.

features.name: <ol>, <ul>, and <li>
features.description: The <ol>, <ul>, and <li> HTML elements represent ordered and unordered lists.

features.name: List style
features.description: The list-style shorthand CSS property and the list-style-image, list-style-position, and list-style-type longhand properties set the position and appearance of a list item's marker.

features.name: Lazy-loading images and iframes
features.description: The loading="lazy" attribute for and

features.name: Lazy-loading media
features.description: The loading="lazy" attribute for

features.name: Local fonts
features.description: The window.queryLocalFonts() method returns an array of locally-installed fonts, each represented by a FontData object.

features.name: Local network access
features.description: The "local-network-access" user permission (and certain actions that imply this permission, such as a fetch() request with { targetAddressSpace: "local" }) allows a site to send requests to servers on a user's local network.

features.name: localStorage and sessionStorage
features.description: The localStorage and sessionStorage APIs store data as key-value pairs. While localStorage persists across sessions, sessionStorage data is discarded when the page is closed.

features.name: Location
features.description: The location global object represents the current page's address. You can use it to get the parts of the address (such as location.hostname or location.pathname) or navigate to another URL.

features.name: Logical assignments
features.description: The logical AND assignment (&&=) and the logical OR assignment (||=) operators short-circuit the respective binary logical operators.

features.name: Logical properties
features.description: CSS logical properties control borders, size, margin, and padding with directions and dimensions relative to the writing mode. For example, in a left to right, top to bottom writing mode, block-end refers to the bottom. Also known as flow relative.

features.name: Long animation frames performance entries
features.description: A long-animation-frame performance entry measures rendering updates that take longer than 50 milliseconds. Also known as LoAFs.

features.name: Long task performance entries
features.description: A longtask performance entry measures tasks that occupy the UI thread for 50 milliseconds or more, a metric for input latency, delayed animations, and other sources of "jank."

features.name: Magnetometer
features.description: The Magnetometer API reads magnetic field sensor data from the device's magnetometer.

features.name: <main>
features.description: The <main> element represents the dominant content of a document. It is commonly used together with <header> and <footer>.

features.name: Managed media source
features.description: The ManagedMediaSource API is a MediaSource where the browser manages the memory of source buffers and may evict data if needed.

features.name: Web app manifest
features.description: A web app manifest file provides metadata about the site. The browser can use the metadata to install the site as a standalone application on the user's device. The metadata usually includes the app's name, icon, description, and ways in which the app wishes to integrate with the device.

features.name: Web app manifest localization
features.description: The _localized suffixed members of the web app manifest set translated names, descriptions, icons, and shortcuts. The browser automatically selects resources based on the user's language and region settings.

features.name: Map (initial support)
features.description: Map objects hold key-value pairs and remember the original insertion order of the keys.

features.name: margin
features.description: The margin CSS property sets space around an element. It is a shorthand for margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom, and margin-left.

features.name: margin-trim
features.description: The margin-trim CSS property removes the margins of child elements when they meet the edges of the container.

features.name: <mark>
features.description: The <mark> element represents text which is marked or highlighted for reference or notation purposes.

features.name: ::marker
features.description: The ::marker CSS pseudo-element selects list item markers for styling numbers or bullets.

features.name: mask-border
features.description: The mask-border CSS property sets how the edges of an element are masked. It is a shorthand for mask-border-outset, mask-border-repeat, mask-border-slice, mask-border-source, and mask-border-width.

features.name: mask-type
features.description: The mask-type CSS property on an SVG <mask> element sets whether the mask is a luminance or alpha mask.

features.name: Masks
features.description: The mask CSS property (and several longhand properties) partially or completely hides an element according to the shape and depth of an image.

features.name: matchMedia
features.description: The window.matchMedia() method checks whether a media query applies to the document.

features.name: Math.sumPrecise()
features.description: The Math.sumPrecise() static method returns the sum of an iterable of numbers. It avoids the precision loss of intermediate partial sums, as found using reduce() or a loop to add together an array of values.

features.name: MathML
features.description: MathML, or the Mathematical Markup Language, describes mathematical notation, such as expressions and formulas. Also known as MathML Core.

features.name: Memory measurement
features.description: The measureUserAgentSpecificMemory() method estimates the memory usage of a web application including all its iframes and workers.

features.name: Media capabilities
features.description: The navigator.mediaCapabilities API queries the encoding and decoding abilities of the device, such as supported codecs, resolutions, and bitrates.

features.name: Media capture
features.description: The navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia() API requests access to devices that produce audio or video streams, such as microphones or video cameras.

features.name: Media playback quality
features.description: The getVideoPlaybackQuality() method of HTMLVideoElement returns metrics that can be used to determine the playback quality of a video, such as how many frames were dropped.

features.name: Media element pseudo-classes
features.description: The :playing, :paused, :seeking, :buffering, :stalled, :muted, and :volume-locked CSS pseudo-classes match <audio> and <video> elements based on their state.

features.name: Media queries
features.description: The @media CSS rule conditionally applies styles based on the output device type, its capabilities, and the user's preferences. Media queries are composed of an optional media type such as screen or print, and one or more mandatory media features, such as prefers-reduced-animations.

features.name: Media query range syntax
features.description: The range syntax of CSS media queries allows you to use mathematical comparison operators such as <, >, <=, and >= to define a range of values for a media query. For example, (400px < width < 1000px) returns true if the viewport width is between 400px and 1000px.

features.name: Media session
features.description: The navigator.mediaSession API integrates with platform UI for media playback. It can be used to set metadata such as title and artwork, and to handle user actions like playing, pausing, or seeking.

features.name: Media source
features.description: The MediaSource API is a custom data source for media elements commonly used for adaptive streaming. Also known as Media Source Extensions (MSE).

features.name: MediaStream recording
features.description: The MediaRecorder API captures data generated by MediaStream or HTMLMediaElement objects for analysis, processing, or saving to disk. Also known as the Media Recording API.

features.name: <menu>
features.description: The <menu> element represents an unordered list of action items (<li>), such as a toolbar. It is a semantic alternative to the <ul> element.

features.name: messageerror
features.description: The messageerror event fires on a target, such as a window or worker, when an incoming message cannot be deserialized. This event can fire for many types of messages, such as cross-document messages or broadcast channel messages.

features.name: <meta>
features.description: The <meta> element represents metadata about the page used by the browser or search engines, including description, keywords, and character sets.

features.name: <meta name="application-title">
features.description: The name="application-title" attribute for the <meta> HTML element sets an installed web application's title bar text.

features.name: Meta refresh
features.description: The <meta http-equiv="refresh"> HTML element and the equivalent Refresh HTTP header trigger a page reload or redirect. They apply only when the page is fully loaded, after other HTTP redirects or scripted redirects that might execute before the page is fully loaded.

features.name: <meta name="text-scale">
features.description: The <meta name="text-scale" content="scale" /> HTML element allows the browser's initial font size to be affected by the operating system text scale settings. The <meta name="text-scale" content="legacy" /> element is the default behavior that respects only browser font-size settings.

features.name: <meta name="theme-color">
features.description: The name="theme-color" attribute for the <meta> HTML element suggests a color that the browser can use to customize the display of the page or the browser user interface.

features.name: <meter>
features.description: The <meter> element represents a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value, typically shown as a progress bar.

features.name: min(), max(), and clamp()
features.description: The min() and max() CSS functions return the minimum or maximum of the arguments, while clamp() clamps a value to a given range.

features.name: min-content and max-content
features.description: The min-content and max-content CSS keywords represent the smallest and largest intrinsic sizes of an element.

features.name: Min and max width and height
features.description: The min-width, min-height, max-width, and max-height CSS properties set the minimum and maximum size of an element.

features.name: mix-blend-mode
features.description: The mix-blend-mode CSS property blends an element's content with its background or parent elements using blend modes like multiply, difference, or color.

features.name: Mixed content handling
features.description: When a document is loaded over HTTPS, browsers ensure that none of the document's resources are loaded over an insecure protocol. Instead, resources that the document attempts to load over an insecure protocol are either loaded over HTTPS or are blocked.

features.name: @mixin
features.description: The @mixin and @apply CSS at-rules define reusable style declaration fragments and apply them inside rules, optionally passing arguments.

features.name: :modal
features.description: The :modal pseudo-class selects elements that put other elements into a non-interactive state, such as a fullscreen element or a <dialog> element used with showModal().

features.name: <link rel="modulepreload">
features.description: The rel="modulepreload" attribute for the <link> HTML element indicates that a module script should be fetched, parsed, and compiled preemptively, and stored for later execution.

features.name: Motion path
features.description: The offset CSS property animates an element along a defined motion path.

features.name: Mouse events
features.description: Mouse events, such as click, mousedown, or mousemove, fire when users interact with an input or pointing device such as a mouse, trackpad, or touchscreen.

features.name: moveBefore()
features.description: The moveBefore() DOM method relocates a node while preserving its state. For example, you can move the active element without losing focus, move an animated element without resetting the animation, or move an iframe without reloading its content.

features.name: Multi-column layout
features.description: Multi-column layout flows an element's content across one or more columns in a single row, without affecting the display property of its children.

features.name: MutationObserver
features.description: The MutationObserver API watches for changes to the DOM tree and calls a callback function when DOM changes occur.

features.name: Named colors
features.description: Some CSS color values can be referenced by name, such as red or limegreen. They stand in for specific RGB color values.

features.name: @namespace
features.description: The @namespace CSS rule sets a default namespace or namespace prefix. Namespace prefixes allow CSS selectors to distinguish elements with the same name but different document types, such as the HTML <a> element and the SVG <a> element.

features.name: <nav>
features.description: The <nav> element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents.

features.name: Navigation API
features.description: The navigation API initiates, intercepts, or modifies browser navigation actions. Not to be confused with the navigator API.

features.name: Navigation precommit handlers
features.description: The precommitHandler callback option to NavigateEvent's intercept() method returns a promise that defers navigation until the promise resolves. You can use this to change the navigation's URL, state, and history before navigation occurs.

features.name: Navigation timing performance entries
features.description: A navigation performance entry measures navigation events, such as loading time or the number of redirects.

features.name: Navigation timing confidence
features.description: The confidence property of a navigation performance entry describes whether the navigation metric is likely to be representative the page's performance (high confidence) or affected by transient conditions, such as browser startup (low confidence).

features.name: Navigator
features.description: The window.navigator API is a generic global object, under which many other, more interesting APIs are located. It doesn't do anything interesting on its own.

features.name: navigator.install()
features.description: The navigator.install() method triggers a request to install a progressive web app.

features.name: Nesting
features.description: CSS nesting allows for shorter selectors, easier reading, and more modularity by nesting rules inside others.

features.name: Network Information
features.description: The navigator.connection API provides information about the network connection a device is using and fires events when the connection type changes.

features.name: Non-cookie storage access
features.description: Non-cookie storage access extends the requestStorageAccess() API to let content in cross-site iframes request access to first-party data beyond cookies.

features.name: :not()
features.description: The :not() functional pseudo-class matches elements that do not match the selectors in its argument.

features.name: Notifications
features.description: The Notification() constructor shows a message to the user, typically using the notification system of the host operating system.

features.name: Notifications from service workers and installed apps
features.description: Notifications via service worker registration's showNotification() method, sent from installed web applications (for example, saved to the Home Screen on Safari for iOS), show a message to the user, typically using the notification system of the host operating system.

features.name: :nth-child()
features.description: The :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements based on their index within a list of elements. The :first-child and :last-child pseudo-classes match the first and last element in a list, and the :only-child pseudo-class matches an element with no siblings.

features.name: :nth-child() of <selector>
features.description: The of syntax for the :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements by the relative position of elements, counted from the first or last sibling matching a selector list.

features.name: :nth-of-type() pseudo-classes
features.description: The :nth-of-type() and :nth-last-of-type() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements based on their position among siblings of the same type. The :first-of-type, :last-of-type, and :only-of-type pseudo-classes match the first, last, and only elements of its type.

features.name: Nullish coalescing
features.description: The nullish coalescing (??) and nullish coalescing assignment (??=) operators return (or assign) its right-hand side operand when its left-hand side operand is null or undefined, and otherwise returns its left-hand side operand.

features.name: Math and numbers
features.description: The number type (and Number object) represents floating-point numbers, such as 42 or -4.201, while the Math API contains mathematical functions and constants. JavaScript can also represent boundless negative and positive values as Infinity or not-a-number as NaN (as in 0 * Infinity).

features.name: Numeric factory functions
features.description: The numeric factory functions, such as CSS.px() or CSS.kHz(), return a CSSUnitValue representing a CSS number value (as in 12px or 440kHz).

features.name: Numeric separators
features.description: To improve readability for numeric literals, underscores (_) can be used as separators. For example, 1_050.95 is equivalent to 1050.95.

features.name: <object>
features.description: The <object> element represents an external resource such as a PDF or SVG document. It was historically used for plugins such as Shockwave Flash.

features.name: object-fit
features.description: The object-fit CSS property sets how images, videos, and other replaced elements are scaled within their container.

features.name: Object.hasOwn()
features.description: The Object.hasOwn() static method checks whether an object has a given property. It's a more robust alternative to the Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty() method.

features.name: Object
features.description: Objects in JavaScript are collections of key-value pairs.

features.name: object-position
features.description: The object-position CSS property places images, videos, and other replaced elements within their boxes.

features.name: object-view-box
features.description: The object-view-box CSS property crops and zooms to an inset area of an image.

features.name: Observable
features.description: The when() method on a event target returns an Observable object, which provides a declarative API for subscribing to and operating on events. It's an alternative to addEventListener() callbacks.

features.name: OES_element_index_uint WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_element_index_uint extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds support for gl.UNSIGNED_INT types to WebGLRenderingContext.drawElements().

features.name: OES_fbo_render_mipmap WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_fbo_render_mipmap extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts attaches any level of a texture to a framebuffer object.

features.name: OES_standard_derivatives WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_standard_derivatives extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds the GLSL derivative functions dFdx, dFdy, and fwidth.

features.name: OES_texture_float WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_float extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: OES_texture_float_linear WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_float_linear extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts adds linear filtering with floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: OES_texture_half_float WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_half_float extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds texture formats with 16-bit (also known as half float) and 32-bit floating-point components.

features.name: OES_texture_half_float_linear WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_half_float_linear extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds linear filtering with half floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: OES_vertex_array_object WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_vertex_array_object extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds vertex array objects (VAOs) which encapsulate vertex array states. These objects keep pointers to vertex data and names for different sets of vertex data.

features.name: OfflineAudioContext
features.description: The OfflineAudioContext API represents an audio processing graph that writes to an AudioBuffer instead of an output device.

features.name: Offscreen canvas
features.description: The OffscreenCanvas API provides a canvas that can be drawn to off screen, with no dependencies on the DOM, which can be used to run heavy rendering operations inside a worker context.

features.name: Oklab and OkLCh
features.description: The Oklab color space expresses colors in terms of lightness and how red/green and blue/yellow a color is, aiming to match how humans perceive colors. OkLCh is a variant of Oklab with polar coordinates. These color spaces can be used with the CSS oklab() and oklch() functions.

features.name: Online status
features.description: The navigator.onLine property is a boolean for whether the browser is connected to some network (though not necessarily the internet). The online and offline events fire when the connection state changes.

features.name: opacity
features.description: The opacity CSS property sets the transparency of an element.

features.name: Opacity (SVG)
features.description: The fill-opacity, and stroke-opacity SVG attributes and CSS properties control the transparency of a stroke or fill of an SVG element.

features.name: OpaqueRange
features.description: The createValueRange() for form elements, such as <textarea> or <input type="text">, gets an OpaqueRange object that represents a live span of text. You can use this for range-based operations on the input text, such as setting custom highlights or placing autocomplete popovers.

features.name: :open
features.description: The :open CSS pseudo-class matches elements that have open states, like <details>, <dialog>, or <select>, based on their state.

features.name: Optional catch binding
features.description: Omit the binding parameter of a catch clause when you don't need information about the exception in a try ... catch statement.

features.name: Orientation Sensor
features.description: The AbsoluteOrientationSensor and RelativeOrientationSensor APIs describe the physical orientation of a device in three-dimensional space, either in relation to the Earth's coordinate system or in relation to the device's own orientation, respectively.

features.name: Origin
features.description: An Origin object represents an origin, as in a scheme, hostname, and port. You can use it to make same-site and same-origin comparisons.

features.name: Origin private file system
features.description: The navigator.storage.getDirectory() method returns a FileSystemDirectoryHandle that is restricted to a specific origin and invisible to the user's actual file system for faster file-based applications, such as SQLite databases.

features.name: outline
features.description: The outline CSS shorthand sets the color, style, and width of a line around an element, outside of the border.

features.name: Outlines
features.description: The outline-color, outline-style, and outline-width and outline-offset CSS properties style a line around an element, outside of the border.

features.name: <output>
features.description: The <output> element represents the result of a calculation, user action, or form entry.

features.name: Overflow media queries
features.description: The overflow-block and overflow-inline CSS media queries set styles based on the way a device displays content that's larger than the viewport or page area. For example, a laptop lets users scroll to reveal content, while a printer displays overflowing content on additional pages.

features.name: overflow-anchor
features.description: The overflow-anchor CSS property sets an element as a possible scroll anchor, reducing unintended scrolling when document changes occur above the current scrollport. This is enabled by default where supported.

features.name: overflow: clip
features.description: The overflow: clip CSS declaration clips an element's overflowing content to the box that's defined by the overflow-clip-margin property. Unlike overflow: hidden, it allows you to hide overflow on one axis while keeping overflow on the other axis visible.

features.name: overflow-clip-margin
features.description: The overflow-clip-margin CSS property sets how far overflow content may appear outside the bounds of an element before it's clipped by effects such as overflow: clip.

features.name: overflow
features.description: The overflow CSS property sets the behavior for when content doesn't fit in an element.

features.name: overflow-wrap
features.description: The overflow-wrap CSS property breaks a line of text onto multiple lines inside the targeted element in an otherwise unbreakable place to prevent overflow. The legacy property is word-wrap.

features.name: overlay
features.description: The overlay CSS property, used as an allow-discrete CSS transition, prevents a top layer element, such as a popover or a <dialog>, from being removed from the top layer before it has finished animating. You can't set the value of the overlay property; only use it as transition property.

features.name: overscroll-behavior
features.description: The overscroll-behavior CSS property disables default scrolling behaviors when the edges of a scrolling area are reached.

features.name: OVR_multiview2 WebGL extension
features.description: The OVR_multiview2 extension for WebGL 2.0 contexts renders into multiple views simultaneously. This especially useful for virtual reality (VR) and WebXR.

The

element represents a paragraph of text.

features.name: padding
features.description: The padding CSS property sets space between an element's edge and its contents. It is a shorthand for padding-top, padding-right, padding-bottom, and padding-left.

features.name: Page breaks
features.description: In printed page layouts, the break-after, break-before, break-inside CSS properties control where printed pages start and end. Also known as pagination or page breaking.

features.name: Page lifecycle
features.description: The page lifecycle API helps you safely handle page suspensions or discards from memory. The freeze and resume events fire when the browser suspends or resumes a page from memory while the document.wasDiscarded property reports whether the page was reloaded after being dropped.

features.name: page-orientation
features.description: The page-orientation CSS property sets the rotation of a page after pagination. This allows pages with the same size declaration to display with different orientations.

features.name: Page selectors
features.description: The :first, :left, and :right pseudo-classes select pages based on their position in sequence after pagination.

features.name: Page setup
features.description: The @page CSS at-rule sets the page-specific dimensions and margins for content such as printed documents, ebooks, or slides.

features.name: Page transition events
features.description: The pageshow and pagehide transition events fire when a document loads or unloads due to a navigation, such as clicking on a link on a page or the back button in a browser.

features.name: Page visibility
features.description: The document.visibilityState and document.hidden properties tell you whether the page is visible to the user (for example, it's not minimized or in a background tab).

features.name: Page visibility state performance entries
features.description: A visibility-state performance entry measures the timing of page visibility state changes, such as when a tab is no longer visible or the user has switched to another app.

features.name: paint()
features.description: The paint() CSS function creates a custom image, drawn using a paint worklet, for an element's background or border.

features.name: paint-order
features.description: The paint-order CSS property sets the z-order of strokes, fills, and (in SVG content) markers. For example, paint-order: markers stroke fill; draws the markers, then stroke on top of markers, then fill on top of both markers and stroke.

features.name: Paint timing performance entries
features.description: A paint performance entry measures the duration of "paint" (also called "render") operations as a page loads. It measures the time to First Paint (FP) and First Contentful Paint (FCP), common metrics for perceived loading times.

features.name: Unsanitized HTML parsing
features.description: The Document.parseHTMLUnsafe() static method parses HTML into a DOM tree, much like the setHTMLUnsafe() DOM method inserts HTML into an existing tree. No sanitization applies, so never call it with user-provided strings.

features.name: Partitioned cookies
features.description: Partitioned cookies allow you to opt a cookie into partitioned storage, with a separate cookie jar per top-level site. Also known as Cookies Having Independent Partitioned State or CHIPS.

features.name: Password credentials
features.description: The PasswordCredential API represents a username and password.

features.name: path()
features.description: The path() CSS shape function creates a shape for clip-path, shape-outside, and the SVG attribute d.

features.name: Payment handler
features.description: The payment handler API registers a web application as a payment handler and responds to payment requests in the browser's user interface, rather than redirecting users to a separate site to complete a payment.

features.name: Payment request
features.description: The PaymentRequest API prompts the user to make a payment through the browser's user interface.

features.name: pdfViewerEnabled
features.description: The navigator.pdfViewerEnabled property is a boolean for whether the browser navigates to and shows a PDF in the browser window or downloads the PDF.

features.name: Performance
features.description: The performance global object and the PerformanceObserver API provide access to performance-related information for the current execution context.

features.name: Periodic background sync
features.description: The periodic background synchronization API fires a recurring periodicsync event in a service worker. You can use this to update data in the background at regular intervals.

features.name: Permissions
features.description: The navigator.permissions API checks whether a permission, such as access to geolocation data, has been granted.

features.name: Permissions policy
features.description: The Permissions-Policy response header and the allow attribute for <iframe> elements sets whether a policy-controlled feature, such as an API, may be used in a document.

features.name: Physical properties
features.description: The physical CSS properties, top, right, bottom, and left, set the inset position of an element relative to the corresponding side of a container determined by the element's position property.

features.name: <picture>
features.description: The <picture> element is used for art direction in responsive images, where a different image is displayed based on the <source> element.

features.name: Picture-in-picture (video)
features.description: The picture-in-picture API allow websites to create a floating, always-on-top video window. Also known as PiP or pop-out video.

features.name: ping
features.description: The ping attribute for <a> elements sets a URL to send a POST request to when the <a> is clicked. This is typically used for outbound link reporting.

features.name: ::placeholder
features.description: The ::placeholder CSS pseudo-element selects help text in <input> and <textarea> elements when no value is set.

features.name: :placeholder-shown
features.description: The :placeholder-shown CSS pseudo-element selects <input> and <textarea> elements when no value is set and the element's placeholder attribute is not empty. Not to be confused with ::placeholder, which selects the placeholder text itself.

features.name: PNG
features.description: The PNG (Portable Network Graphics) image format is a raster graphics file format with animation, alpha transparency, and lossless compression.

features.name: pointer-events
features.description: The pointer-events CSS property sets whether a user can interact with an element using a mouse, touch, or other pointing input device.

features.name: Pointer Events
features.description: Pointer events, such as pointerdown, and the PointerEvent API, represent general pointing inputs, from a wide range of devices, such as a mouse, pen or stylus, or touch with one or more fingers. Not to be confused with the pointer-events CSS property.

features.name: Pointer lock
features.description: Provides access to raw mouse movement by locking the target of mouse events to a single element and hiding the mouse cursor.

features.name: Popover
features.description: The popover HTML attribute creates an overlay to display content on top of other page content. Popovers can be shown declaratively using HTML, or using the showPopover() method.

features.name: popover="hint"
features.description: The popover="hint" global HTML attribute creates a popover that is subordinate to popovers with a popover="auto" attribute. You can use this to create tooltips that don't dismiss auto popovers.

features.name: Position
features.description: The position CSS property sets the origin position of an element to an element, the element's scrollport, or the viewport.

features.name: postMessage
features.description: The postMessage() global method sends cross-origin messages to windows and workers, including popups and iframes. Also known as cross-document messaging.

features.name: <pre>
features.description: The <pre> element represents a block element of preformatted text that is presented exactly as written, including all white space.

features.name: prefers-color-scheme media query
features.description: The prefers-color-scheme CSS media query sets styles based on the requested color scheme, light or dark.

features.name: prefers-contrast media query
features.description: The prefers-contrast CSS media query sets styles based on whether the user prefers more or less contrast, the difference between foreground and background colors.

features.name: prefers-reduced-data media query
features.description: The prefers-reduced-data CSS media query detects whether the user has a preference for using less network traffic. For example, you can use this media query to avoid loading large font files and use a system font instead.

features.name: prefers-reduced-motion media query
features.description: The prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query sets styles based on whether the user prefers to minimize the amount of non-essential animations on the device, such as scrolling, panning, zooming, and strobing.

features.name: prefers-reduced-transparency media query
features.description: The prefers-reduced-transparency CSS media query sets styles based on whether the user prefers to reduce the amount of transparent effects on their device, for example to improve contrast and legibility.

features.name: Preloading responsive images
features.description: The imagesrcset and imagesizes attributes with the rel="preload" attribute for the <link> HTML element starts fetching responsive images before they're found in the body of the document.

features.name: Presentation API
features.description: The Presentation API shows or controls content on another display, such as a network-connected TV or projector.

features.name: preservesPitch
features.description: The preservesPitch property for <audio> or <video> adjusts the pitch of audio to sound more natural when the playback rate is faster or slower than the default.

features.name: window.print()
features.description: The window.print() method opens the browser's print dialog.

features.name: print-color-adjust
features.description: The print-color-adjust CSS property sets whether styles of printed pages should be adjusted to use less ink, in cases such as light text on a dark background.

features.name: Print events
features.description: An alternative to @media print queries, the beforeprint and afterprint events allow you to change the page for printing and restore the page after printing.

features.name: Private click measurement
features.description: The attributionsourceid and attributiondestination attributes for <a> elements measure clicks across websites without associating a click to a specific session. Not to be confused with attribution reporting. Also known as PCM.

features.name: Profiler
features.description: The Profiler API records data about the execution of a page, which you can send to a server for later analysis. Also known as self-profiling.

features.name: <progress>
features.description: The <progress> element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.

features.name: progress()
features.description: The progress() CSS function returns a ratio for the relative position of one value between two other values, clamped between 0 and 1. You can use it to interpolate a value for other calculations.

features.name: Promise (initial support)
features.description: A promise represents an asynchronous operation which eventually succeeds or fails.

features.name: Promise.allSettled()
features.description: The Promise.allSettled() static method waits for an array of promises to settle (resolve or reject).

features.name: Promise.any()
features.description: The Promise.any() static method returns a promise that fulfills as soon as the first of an iterable of promises fulfills, with that promise's value. Otherwise, it rejects with an AggregateError when all of the promises have rejected.

features.name: Promise finally()
features.description: The promise finally() method executes a function when the promise settles (resolves or rejects).

features.name: Promise.try()
features.description: The Promise.try() static method returns a promise that takes a callback of any kind (returns or throws, synchronously or asynchronously) and wraps its result in a Promise.

features.name: Promise.withResolvers()
features.description: The Promise.withResolvers() static method is an alternative to the Promise() constructor that returns both the promise and resolution functions. You can use this to access resolve and reject outside the scope of the executor function.

features.name: Proxy and Reflect
features.description: The Proxy and Reflect JavaScript built-ins intercept and define custom behavior for fundamental language operations (such as property lookup, assignment, enumeration, or function invocation).

features.name: Push messages
features.description: The Push API subscribes to and receives server-initiated messages. Subscribers receive pushed messages in the background, even after periods inactive or offline.

features.name: <q>
features.description: The <q> element represents a short inline quotation.

features.name: Q unit
features.description: The Q CSS length unit is an absolute length anchored to the physical measurement of quarter-millimeters. 1Q is equivalent to 1/40 of 1 centimeter.

features.name: queueMicrotask()
features.description: The queueMicrotask() method schedules a function to run after the currently running synchronous JavaScript finishes but before returning to the event loop.

features.name: Quotes
features.description: The quotes CSS property sets the quotation marks inserted via the content CSS property or <q> element.

features.name: random()
features.description: The random() CSS function chooses a random numeric value within a specified range. This allows for dynamic, randomized styling using CSS.

features.name: rcap unit
features.description: The rcap CSS length unit is a font-relative length equal to the value of the cap unit on the root element. Cap-height is approximately equal to the height of a capital Latin letter.

features.name: rch unit
